question.leadin: During this war, UN forces were set back to a 140-mile defense line known as the "Pusan Perimeter" due to multiple defeats by the KPA.
question.text: Name this 1950s war that never ended with a peace treaty, but instead with the establishment of the DMZ. The U.S. and Soviet Union divided the namesake country of this war along the 38th parallel.
question.clue: The Armistice Agreement that ended this war was signed shortly after Joseph Stalin's death caused a withdrawal of Soviet support.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Asian political families.
swap.text: One member of this country's Kim family was ostracized after trying to visit Tokyo Disneyland and was mysteriously assassinated in 2017.
swap.answerHtml: <u>North Korea</u> (or <u>Democratic People’s Republic of Korea</u>; or <u>DPRK</u>; do not accept or prompt on Republic of Korea)
swap.clue: One leader threatened this country with "fire and fury like the world has never seen."

question.leadin: Name these places identified with the Korean War.
question.text: This village in the DMZ was the location of the peace talks between the two sides, and talks still go on just outside this village.
question.clue: This village which hosted a more famous conference that led to the armistice between United Nations forces and communists in 1953 during the Korean War.

swap.leadin: Give the following about medieval Asian warfare.
swap.text: In the 16th century, Yi Sun-sin perfected the design of the turtle ships used by the Joseon dynasty to defend this Asian peninsula from the invading Japanese navy. One modern country on this peninsula has capital Seoul.
swap.clue: The "Three Kingdoms" of this region included Baekje, Silla, and Goguryeo.

question.text: The Three Kingdoms period consisted of clashes between the Silla, Goguryeo (koh-KUR-yoh), and this Korean state in the southwest, which was governed from Hansong and was ruled by Geunchogo (gwen-CHOH-goh).
question.clue: This kingdom absorbed all of the lands of the Mahan confederacy, thus seizing all of the present-day Jeolla ("jul-lah") region, under its great ruler Geunchogo ("geun-choh-goh").

swap.text: Yi fought for the independence of this longest Korean dynasty, which lasted from 1392 to 1897. The Hall of Worthies was a circle of scholars formed by this dynasty's emperor Sejong the Great, who personally created the Korean alphabet of Hangul.
swap.clue: Members of the yangban (yong-bon) class were killed by followers of the "Eastern Learning" Donghak religion during this dynasty.

question.leadin: The first president of this nation was overthrown in the April Revolution because he rigged the election.
question.text: Name this nation that disputes the possession of the Liancourt Rocks with an eastern neighbor.
question.answerHtml: South Korea (accept Republic of Korea, prompt on Korea)
question.clue: This country's first female leader led it from 2013 until her 2017 impeachment.

swap.text: During the war, U.N. pilots also referred to the northwest of Korea as "[these planes] Alley," since Americans F-86 Sabres often encountered Soviet aircraft there.
swap.clue: During the war, the northwest of North Korea gained this nickname from UN forces, due to the presence of Soviet fighter planes here. Along the Yalu River, this region was the site of many dogfights.

question.leadin: Identify the following about the history of Buddhism in Korea.
question.text: Warrior monks in the Righteous Army were active participants in the first of these events. After a brief exile, Admiral Yi Sun-shin led his forces to victory in the Battle of Myeongnyang (myung-n'YAHNG) during one of these events.
question.answerHtml: Japanese invasions of Korea [or Toyotomi Hideyoshi's invasions of the Korean peninsula; or Imjin War; or Wanil Korean Campaign; or Bunroku no ek; or Keichō no eki; or Kara iri]
question.clue: An opponent of one of these was Admiral Yi Sun-shin, who utilized turtle ships.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Asian dynasties.
swap.text: Ending with the Japanese annexation in 1910, this dynasty ruled Korea for over five hundred years from the capital Hanyang, and it saw the creation of the Hangul phonetic alphabet.
swap.clue: It attempted to curb the power of its scholar officials in four "literati purges," and eventually its ruling intelligentsia devolved into the Sirhak and Tonghak movements.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Korean War.
question.text: Holding virtually dictatorial powers, this man was the president of during the Korean War.
question.clue: Jimmie Leach observed his crackdown of the April 3rd uprising on Jeju Island.

swap.text: This longest Korean dynasty was later established when its King Taejo ("TAY-jo") overthrew a Goryeo ("GORE-yo") king loyal to the Mongols. Sejong the Great developed the hangul alphabet during this dynasty.
swap.clue: As he died, a military leader of this kingdom instructed, "Beat my war drums. Do not announce my death."

question.text: The Korean peninsula was introduced to Buddhism from China in the fourth century CE by Sundo, who mainly proselytized in this kingdom. Baekje, Silla, and this kingdom comprised the Korean Samhan.
question.clue: Some of the best-preserved art of this kingdom survives in the tomb of Dong Shou at a complex at Anak.

swap.leadin: This naval commander destroyed approximately 100 enemy ships at the Battle of Hansan Island without losing a single ship of his own.
swap.text: Name this admiral who leveraged the regular reversal of the tide to win the Battle of Myeongnyang ("myung-nyahng"). This undefeated Korean admiral used turtle ships to defend Korea during the Imjin War.

question.leadin: The poetry contained in this admiral's War Diary is widely considered a classic of Korean literature.
question.text: Name this victor at the Battle of Noryang, who built early ironclads called "turtle ships" to defend against a Japanese invasion during the Imjin War.
question.clue: This naval commander, often considered one of the best in history. After being fatally shot by a bullet at the Battle of Noryang, he instructed his soldiers to beat the war drums instead of announcing his death.

swap.leadin: The grievances that led to this event were later addressed by the Gabo Reform.
swap.text: Name this anti-yangban, anti-foreigner revolt that took place in 1894 and served as the catalyst for the Sino-Japanese war.
swap.clue: Mostly focused on the yangban class of the nobility, this movement drew from the earlier "Flower Boys" groups active in the Silla Kingdom.

question.text: This term was used to refer to the landholding class in the Joseon Dynasty, who were further divided into the munban and muban groups.
question.clue: Members of this Joseon noble, scholarly class were expected to be knowledgeable in the Confucian classics. To enter this class, one had to perform well on the gwageo civil service exam.

swap.text: This institution of scholars, established by Sejong, is credited with the invention of Hangul. Several of this institution's members were part of the "six martyred ministers" killed by King Sejo, who disbanded it.
swap.clue: This institution whose yangban("yong-bahn") scholars largely focused on compiling the Hunminjeongeum ("hoon-meen-chong-um"), a treatise on the Hangul writing system.

question.leadin: It began when Wang Kon united the kingdoms of Goguryeo, Silla and Baekje.
question.text: Name this Korean dynasty that reigned from 918 to 1392.
question.clue: Twenty-nine women from hojeok ("HO-juck") families were married to this dynasty's founder, Wang Geon ("gun").

swap.text: Prior to being mostly reversed by Lee Myung-bak, Kim Dae-jung's Sunshine Policy helped repair South Korea's relations with the regime of this co-producer of the assuredly tasteful film Diary of a Girl Student, a North Korean dictator with crazy hair and crazier everything else.
swap.clue: His "Sunshine policy" tried to bolster the software industry, and he once abducted a movie director to shoot a socialist Godzilla flick.
